enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1041 PM MDT Tue Oct 27 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 947 PM MDT Tue Oct 27 2026

 - A brief stretch of drier weather through Wednesday before rain
   chances return Thursday through the weekend. A few storms will
   be capable of heavy rain and localized flooding. Halloween
   looks mostly dry.

 - Typical temperatures for the end of October with lowland highs
   in the mid to upper 70s, becoming slightly cooler this 
   weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 947 PM MDT Tue Oct 27 2026

Flow aloft turns more SW for Wed, bringing moisture back into the
region from the south. A few showers and storms look to develop in
the afternoon over Hudspeth and the Otero Mesa. Gusts to 40 mph 
and brief downpours are possible during the afternoon. Mostly dry 
conditions are forecast for El Paso and SW New Mexico with light 
S-SW winds.

Moisture levels rise further for Thu as a shortwave trough pushes
through NW Mexico. PWs climb towards 1" during the day, focusing
over SE areas for rain chances and flash flood concerns. Scattered
showers and isolated storms are forecast with repeated rounds of
activity possible into the overnight. Isolated rain amounts of 
1-2" are likely through Thu night, favoring E of the US 54
corridor. Most likely rainfall is 0.1-0.25". Gusty winds and small
hail are possible as instability and shear will be low compared to
what we saw last week with our severe event. The flood threat
lowers as you go west. This system exits Fri AM with a weaker 
shortwave arriving behind it Fri night. This will bring more
scattered showers mainly to western areas Fri afternoon and night.
The flood threat shouldn't be as high late Fri with this
disturbance with generally light rain rates expected. 

Halloween dries out as a weak ridge translates over the region.
Mostly cloudy skies are forecast for Sat with seasonal temps and
light SW winds. Another Pacific trough moves into the Desert SW on
Sun, bringing record moisture to the region. PWs are modeled to
reach near 1.2", which is 3-4 std deviations above normal 
(0.45"). Rain chances and the flood threat will favor western 
areas and the high terrain through Sun night with lower chances 
for Texas. Breezy W winds also look to accompany the low Sun/Mon 
with cooler temps behind the Pacific front. A quiet, dry stretch 
of weather is modeled into the middle of next week as upper
ridging builds from the west.

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 947 PM MDT Tue Oct 27 2026

VFR conditions prevail through the period. Mainly SKC with FEW-SCT
CU around KELP developing during the afternoon. S winds near 
10kts for KTCS after 18z, otherwise AOB 6kts for all terminals. 
Isolated TS east of KELP in the afternoon.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1125 AM MDT Tue Oct 27 2026

No fire weather concerns are forecast for the period as afternoon
RH values stay well above critical thresholds with light winds.
Temperatures will be seasonal. Little to no rain chances are
forecast for today and tomorrow, but widespread showers and 
thunderstorms are in the forecast for Thursday, Friday, and 
Sunday. Vent rates will range poor to good each afternoon. The 
weakest vent rates will be Thursday and Friday.
